drivingQuestion: Why would one need artifice for a female, which has no firstborn sanctity?
outcomeNote: The clause is assigned to a consecrated mother.

segments.he: אִם נְקֵבָה זִבְחֵי שְׁלָמִים — נְקֵבָה מִי קָא קָדְשָׁה בִּבְכוֹרָה? סֵיפָא אָתְיָא לִבְהֵמָה דְּהֶקְדֵּשׁ.
segments.en: § The latter clause of the mishna teaches that in a case where the owner of an animal that is going to give birth to its firstborn says: «If it is female,» it is designated as «a peace offering,» then if the animal gave birth to a female, it will be sacrificed as a peace offering. The Gemara asks: «Does a female» animal become «consecrated» with «firstborn» status, such that the owner must designate the fetus as a peace offering in order to circumvent the obligation of the firstborn? The sanctity of the firstborn takes effect only upon male animals. The Gemara answers: «The latter clause» of the mishna «comes» to discuss the offspring of «an animal consecrated» as a sin offering. Since the offspring of a sin offering is put to death, the owner may wish to employ artifice to circumvent the sanctity of the mother by consecrating the fetus with a different sanctity.

moves.summary: A female is not a firstborn
moves.about: a female is never sanctified as a firstborn, so why would artifice be needed

moves.summary: The latter clause concerns an animal consecrated (e.g., as a sin offering)
